title: Define the service contract
summary: Specify inputs, results and failure behaviour without prematurely selecting a platform.

sections.label: Questions to resolve
items: Supported reference/task classes and unsupported-input response.
Output schema/version, supported components and compatibility.
Generation, saving, application and execution as separate actions.
Progress, clarification, preview and failure information visible to the user.
Repeated submissions, retry, cancellation and partial completion.
Caller/tenant permissions, job state and artifact storage.

sections.label: Sync versus async
sections.text: Base the choice on observed duration/variance, caller timeouts, clarification and recovery needs. Asynchronous request-reply with a job/status resource is a candidate pattern, not an established requirement.

sections.label: Minimal UX during study
sections.text: Full experience design may stay deferred. A lightweight sketch of clarification, preview and failure behaviour can still inform feasibility and effort.

sections.label: Illustrative proposed flow
sections.text:
Reference -> input checks -> bounded generation -> candidate validation
usable -> artifact + validation evidence
incomplete -> clarification
unsupported / failed / limits reached -> explicit outcome or assistance
Application/execution is separately specified.

sections.label: Candidate evidence
sections.text: Identify input/reference version, candidate artifact, workflow/skill/model versions and checks. This evidence design does not require exposing every implementation detail in product UI.

basis: Ticket-scoped recommendation; not an implemented workplace capability
confidence: Moderate for fit; workplace benefit unknown

catalog.applicability: Use this when a study must specify what a proposed service accepts, returns and does on failure before a platform is chosen. Decide sync versus async from observed duration, caller timeouts and recovery needs, and keep generation, saving, application and execution as separate actions.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
